BEIJING, Oct 28 (Reuters) – Liu Yandong, China’s former vice premier and a former member of the elite Politburo, died in Beijing on Wednesday, state-run Xinhua news agency said.

Born in November 1945, Liu was 80.

Norway’s premier says call with Putin was effort to present European views

Reuters

28 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

OSLO, Oct 28 (Reuters) – Norway’s prime minister defended on Wednesday a three-way call with Vladimir Putin and Finland’s president, saying it was intended to ensure the Russian leader heard European as well as US views.

Tuesday’s call between Russia’s Putin, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian premier Jonas Gahr Stoere broke a longstanding practice among Western European leaders of shunning direct contact with the Kremlin, and was criticised by allies including Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen.

The 90-minute call came ahead of what are expected to be the first face-to-face talks since February between Ukrainian and Russian officials, in Abu Dhabi next month.

Show Full Article

“We (Stubb and I) were focused on looking forward, what must happen for this war to not continue endlessly for months, with people dying … and it is even more difficult to find a solution,” Stoere told public broadcaster NRK.

“I don’t think (Putin) will change his mind, but he gets to hear our position very clearly. I am worried that some of these messages do not reach him when the Americans talk to him,” he said.

Norway, said Stoere, was keen to introduce de-escalation steps such as stopping attacks on energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine, halting strikes on ships exporting Ukrainian grain and conducting prisoner-of-war exchanges.

Asked whether there could be peace without Ukraine ceding territory, Stoere said: “Today Russia controls nearly 20% (of Ukrainian territory). Ukraine will never sign a deal that recognises that they have lost territory, but whether they can take the current frontline as a reality and as a starting point, that is a different question.”

“And the big question is what kind of security guarantees can there be for the country (Ukraine) after a peace deal? Putin recognises that this is the big question.”

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said Tuesday’s call offered nothing new on the Ukraine conflict, and that European countries were simply seeking a role in the negotiation process.

(Reporting by Gwladys Fouche in Oslo; Editing by Terje Solsvik, Louise Rasmussen, Aidan Lewis)

At least 10 people dead in Spain after two high-speed trains collide

Reuters

28 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MADRID, Oct 28 (Reuters) – At least 10 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, regional authorities said.

Footage from regional Castilla-La Mancha Television showed a derailed train with at least one carriage remaining on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line.

Miguel, a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident.

Show Full Article

“We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train – I imagine it must have been the other one,” he said.

DEATH TOLL LIKELY TO RISE

Castilla-La Mancha region spokesperson Esther Padilla said the number of casualties was likely to rise.

“The latest confirmed figure is 10 dead, but we know it is going to increase. Very likely we will be talking about a higher number,” Padilla said, adding that several carriages had plunged down an embankment.

She said 147 people had been travelling on the Iryo train and 397 on the Renfe train.

The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to the same operators on the same line that killed 46 people.

That crash in January, which occurred after a train derailed and smashed into an oncoming train near Adamuz, in Cordoba province, triggered a debate about the level of investment in railway maintenance in recent years.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s agenda, published on the Spanish government’s website, had been cleared for the day. The opposition People’s Party also cancelled all campaign events ahead of a snap election on November 29, a spokesperson said.

“Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families,” Sanchez said on X.

The Renfe and Iryo trains crashed just after 9 a.m. (0800 GMT), causing two Iryo wagons to derail, a spokesperson for the Castilla La Mancha region said, adding that the cause was not yet clear.

Rail operator Adif said the incident occurred on the line from Madrid to Seville.

Manuel Galan, the mayor of the nearby town of Urda, told Cadena SER that emergency services had asked the town council to prepare emergency facilities, including a sports hall, to accommodate passengers and the injured.

(Reporting by David Latona, Emma Pinedo, Mireia Merino, Corina Pons, Victoria Waldersee, Benjamin Mejias and Joan Faus; Writing by Charlie Devereux; Editing by Toby Chopra and Alison Williams)

Indonesian students protest over forest fires, Prabowo policies

Reuters

28 October, 2026 04:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Stanley Widianto JAKARTA, Oct 28 (Reuters) – Hundreds of Indonesian students and civil society groups staged protests on Wednesday in cities including the capital Jakarta against President Prabowo Subianto’s policies, including the handling of ongoing forest fires.

Worsened by the El Niño weather pattern that leaves peatland vulnerable to fires, Indonesia has been faced with its worst forest fires, and resulting haze, in 11 years, increasing respiratory illnesses and polluting the air of neighbouring countries Malaysia and Singapore.

Protesters crowded a Jakarta landmark roundabout, with some wearing gas masks, holding up signs protesting over forest fires and demanding the government designate the blazes as a national disaster.

Show Full Article

Some carried signs that said “If we burn, you burn with us,” and held up the three-finger sign of protest – references to the The Hunger Games movie that has been adopted as a symbol by many youth protest movements globally.

Anggi Aurien, 28, had been wearing a gas mask for three hours at the landmark, protesting about the forest fires that have killed wildlife.

“Animals don’t have a mind of their own. If we kill them, what’s the difference between us and them?” she said.

Other signs included photos of the orangutan, which bears the brunt of the fires, and a cardboard cutout of Prabowo.

Other students, including from the University of Indonesia, were blocked by dozens of police and military personnel, leading to some scuffles.

“Revolution! Revolution!” protesters chanted.

Ezra Al Barra, a student from the University of Padjadjaran, said the fires were “our collective anger,” adding students came from other regions outside Jakarta.

Students also rallied in Makassar, in South Sulawesi, and Bandung, in West Java, with similar demands. Dozens of them on motorbikes filled the main roads.

Protesters called for the the government halt spending on populist programmes such as Prabowo’s free meals scheme, among other demands.

Syahganda Nainggolan, chief of the government’s communications office, urged calm but said the government welcomed the protests and was open to input.

PRABOWO’S POPULARITY

The protests, the second in a week, came as Prabowo’s approval ratings had fallen steadily since late last year, according to surveys by Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting, two years into his presidency.

Indonesia has prosecuted companies allegedly linked to the fires and tried methods of modifying the weather to induce rain.

Indonesia’s last major protest took place in August, when hundreds were detained.

In 2025, weeks-long nationwide protests broke out in Indonesia after the police killing of a motorcycle taxi driver, with several more people killed during the unrest.

(Reporting by Stanley Widianto, Johan Purnomo, Heru Asprihanto and Ananda Teresia; Editing by David Stanway and Alex Richardson)
